sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Origin**: Founded by **Karam Shah** as a religious sect, later transformed into a militant peasant movement under his son **Tipu Shah**.
• **Ideology**: Based on the principles of **equality, brotherhood, and resistance** against the arbitrary exactions of the British-backed zamindari system.
• **Geographic Focus**: Primarily centered in the **Sherpur region** of Mymensingh district (now in Bangladesh).
• **Key Metric**: The movement was a direct reaction to the **Permanent Settlement (1793)**, which empowered zamindars to extract exorbitant rents from the Hajong and Garo tribes.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Founded by Karam Shah; focused on religious syncretism and moral upliftment.
Contextual background for the later militant phase.
Led by Tipu Shah (1825-1835); armed resistance against zamindars.
Economic exploitation, high rents, and lack of legal protection.
Direct UPSC focus: Peasant uprisings against colonial land policy.

items.definition: The charismatic leader who organized the peasants into a fighting force, captured Sherpur, and established an independent administrative structure.
The primary tribal communities that formed the backbone of the Pagal Panthi movement due to their displacement and economic marginalization.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Parallel Government**: Tipu Shah established a 'court' to settle disputes, effectively challenging British judicial authority.
• **Armed Resistance**: The movement utilized guerrilla tactics to attack zamindari offices and police outposts.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Lack of centralized coordination, superior British military technology, and eventual suppression by the colonial state.
• **Legacy**: Served as a precursor to later agrarian movements like the Indigo Revolt and the Tebhaga movement.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'PAGAL' (Pagal Panthi, Area: Garo/Hajong, Area: Mymensingh, Leader: Tipu, Cause: Land/Rent).
• **Decoded Meaning**: P-Pagal, A-Area (Mymensingh), G-Garo/Hajong, A-Armed, L-Leader (Tipu).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Pagal Panthi' with 'Faraizi' or 'Wahabi' movements. Remember: Pagal Panthi was localized in Mymensingh, whereas Faraizi was a broader Islamic revivalist movement.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Subaltern Resistance' to describe the Pagal Panthi movement, highlighting the agency of tribal peasants against colonial-feudal nexus.

keyTakeaways: The movement was a fusion of religious identity and agrarian economic grievances.
It represents the early 19th-century resistance against the Permanent Settlement's negative externalities.
The movement successfully challenged the legitimacy of the British-backed zamindari judicial system.
